cards.text: This is a Maskil of Asaph, the chief of the Levites David appointed to praise the LORD before the ark (1 Chronicles 16:4-5). He opens like a man tapping the mic: “Give ear, O my people, to my instruction; listen to the words of my mouth.” Then he says he'll open his mouth in parables and speak of things hidden from the beginning.

cards.question: Asaph is about to share things hidden from the beginning. How did these things reach him and his people?
Asaph says his people will keep these stories hidden from their children.

cards.text: Not a chance. They'll tell the next generation the praises of the LORD, His might and the wonders He has performed, and nobody's locking this in a drawer, friend, because trust me, I KNOW what happens in drawers.

God set up a testimony in Jacob and a law in Israel, and He commanded the fathers to teach them to their children. The goal is that the coming generation knows them, even children not born yet, and tells THEIR children too, like a relay race where nobody's allowed to drop the baton.

cards.question: Why does God want every generation passing these things down?

answers.text: So they'd put their confidence in God
So the nations would fear them
So they'd never need a king

cards.text: Then Asaph names who he hopes the next generation WON'T turn out like. Lean in, friend.

cards.question: Asaph hopes the coming generation won't turn out like whom?

cards.text: Their fathers were “a stubborn and rebellious generation, whose heart was not loyal, whose spirit was not faithful to God.” Picture a family cookie recipe with a note at the bottom: “Bake these. Don't be like Grandpa.”
Then Asaph brings up the archers of Ephraim, one of Israel's tribes (Numbers 1:32-33). Bows in hand, day of battle, here we go… and they turn back.

cards.question: Asaph says the tribe of Ephraim ___ the wonders God had shown them.
Asaph says the archers of Ephraim kept God's covenant and lived by His law.

cards.text: So Asaph walks them back through everything they forgot. It starts in the land of Egypt, in the region of Zoan, where God worked wonders right in front of their fathers.

cards.question: Then God brings His people to the sea. What does He do with it?

answers.text: Splits it and brings them through
Dries it up with the sun

cards.text: “He set the waters upright like a wall.” WATER, standing UP, like a WALL, friend, and I can't get a ball of dough to stand up for ten seconds.

cards.question: By day God led His people with a cloud. All night He led them with a light of ___.
Out in the wilderness, God split the rocks, and out came ___.

cards.text: Streams from the stone, water flowing down like rivers, drink as abundant as the seas. From a ROCK, friend, and the only thing I ever got out of a rock was a chipped edge.
After all those wonders, the very next line starts with “But.” They kept right on sinning, rebelling in the desert against the Most High.

cards.question: In the desert, the people willfully tested God by ___ the food they craved.

cards.text: They spoke against God, saying, “Can God really prepare a table in the wilderness?” Friend, this is the God who pulled rivers out of a rock.

cards.question: The people admit God struck the rock and water gushed out. What do they doubt He can do next?

cards.text: Their exact words: “But can He also give bread or supply His people with meat?” That's like watching me stamp a perfect cookie and going, “Okay, but can he do a SECOND one?”

cards.question: When the LORD heard what the people said, He was filled with ___.
Asaph says God's anger flared because the people did not believe God or rely on His salvation.

cards.text: Yet look what God does next. He commands the clouds above and opens the doors of the heavens.

cards.question: What does God rain down on the people from the open doors of the heavens?

cards.text: Asaph says, “Man ate the bread of angels; He sent them food in abundance.” They asked whether God could do bread, and He went straight to the ANGEL bread.
Then He stirred the east wind from the heavens and drove the south wind by His might.

cards.question: The people also asked about meat. What does God rain down on them next?
God brought the birds down far from the camp, so the people had to go out and hunt for them.

cards.text: He rained meat on them like dust, birds like the sand of the sea, and they ate until they were well filled. Ask for one cookie, get buried under the WHOLE batch.

cards.question: The people are eating with the food still in their mouths. What happens next?

cards.text: He put to death their strongest and subdued the young men of Israel. A heavy moment, friend.
In spite of all this, they kept on sinning, and despite His wonderful works, they did not believe. So He ended their days in futility and their years in sudden terror.

cards.question: When God slew them, the people would ___ Him.

cards.text: They remembered that God was their Rock, that God Most High was their Redeemer. Their ROCK, friend, the same God who split the rocks for them in the wilderness.

cards.question: Asaph says the people's hearts were loyal when they turned back to God.

cards.text: They deceived Him with their mouths and lied to Him with their tongues, and their hearts were disloyal to Him. That's texting the group chat that you're on your way while you're still under the covers.

cards.question: The people's hearts are disloyal to God. What does God do?

answers.text: Waits for them to bring an offering
Sends a prophet to warn them

cards.question: Asaph says God often restrained His anger and did not unleash His full wrath.
What does Asaph say God remembered about His people?

cards.text: They forgot what He had done, but He remembered they were but flesh, a passing breeze that does not return, and as a stamper who got remembered after years in a drawer, I'm not crying, YOU'RE crying. Stick around, friend, because Asaph's not done telling this one.
